competency: Design pattern recognition models, rule expert systems, and NLP pipelines
successCriteria: Creates multi-factor criteria: Reading level (Beginner/Intermediate), Genre (Sci-Fi/History/Mystery), Length (<100 pages vs 100+).
Fills all 12 combinations with explicit book recommendations.
Explains why combinatorial explosion occurs when adding more input features.
scaffoldSupport: Pre-formatted 3-variable decision matrix grid.
extensionChallenge: Calculate number of rules needed if 4 features each have 3 possible values (3^4 = 81 rules).
sourceCitation: CBSE Class 7 AI Curriculum, Unit 2, p. 30

title: Analyze the social and economic significance of Prashastis and copper plate land grants
subject: Social Science
competency: Evaluate medieval Indian political institutions, trade routes, and Mughal administration
successCriteria: Explains nature of Prashastis written by court Brahmanas praising rulers.
Examines copper plate seals granting tax-exempt land (Brahmadeya) to scholars and temples.
Evaluates why historians must corroborate Prashastis with independent archaeological evidence.
scaffoldSupport: Photograph of authentic Chola copper plate ring with royal seal.
extensionChallenge: Compare Kalhanas critical historical chronicle Rajatarangini with standard court Prashastis.
sourceCitation: NCERT Grade 7 Our Pasts - II, Chapter 2, pp. 18-20

title: Examine architectural symmetry and water channels in Mughal Charbagh gardens
subject: Social Science
competency: Evaluate medieval Indian political institutions, trade routes, and Mughal administration
successCriteria: Sketches 4-quadrant Charbagh layout divided by intersecting water channels.
Identifies famous examples: Humayuns Tomb, Shalimar Bagh, Taj Mahal.
Explains how Persian garden geometry reflected paradise symbology and imperial order.
scaffoldSupport: Charbagh geometric layout stencil and aerial diagram.
extensionChallenge: Analyze how Mughal architects incorporated trabeate and arcuate engineering into red sandstone domes.
sourceCitation: NCERT Grade 7 Our Pasts - II, Chapter 5 (Rulers and Buildings), pp. 62-67
